ledger.title: The formation of black holes in general relativity
ledger.venue: The Twelfth Marcel Grossmann Meeting (MG12), World Scientific, pp. 24-34 (2012)
ledger.evidence_excerpt: arXiv abstract (via INSPIRE): 'The subject of this work is the formation of black holes in pure general relativity, by the focusing of incoming gravitational waves. The theorems established in this monograph constitute the first foray into the long time dynamics of general relativity in the large, that is, when the initial data are no longer confined to a suitably small neighborhood of Minkowskian data. The theorems are general, no symmetry conditions on the initial data being imposed.'

ledger.title: Regularity of the future event horizon in perturbations of Kerr
ledger.evidence_excerpt: Abstract: 'The goal of the paper is to show that the event horizons of the spacetimes constructed in [KS], see also [KS-Schw], in the proof of the nonlinear stability of slowly rotating Kerr spacetimes K(a0,m0), are necessarily smooth null hypersurfaces. ledger.title: Global aspects of the Cauchy problem in general relativity
ledger.evidence_excerpt: Springer abstract: 'It is shown that, given any set of initial data for Einstein's equations which satisfy the constraint conditions, there exists a development of that data which is maximal in the sense that it is an extension of every other development. These maximal developments form a well-defined class of solutions of Einstein's equations. Any solution of Einstein's equations which has a Cauchy surface may be embedded in exactly one such maximal development.'

ledger.title: The formation of a weak null singularity in the interior of generic rotating black holes
ledger.evidence_excerpt: Abstract: 'Given a characteristic initial value problem with smooth data representing a dynamical event horizon settling down to that of Kerr in the subextremal, strictly rotating range with suitable upper and lower bounds, we prove that a weak null singularity forms, across which the spacetime metric is continuously extendible but not Lipschitz extendible. The bulk of the proof is a stability argument showing that a dynamical Teukolsky field can be approximated by a linear Teukolsky field, whose linear instability was proved in previous works.'

ledger.title: Lipschitz inextendibility of weak null singularities from curvature blow-up
ledger.venue: arXiv:2409.18838 (v2, Nov 2025), 25 pages; accepted for publication in Inventiones Mathematicae (per arXiv comment)
ledger.evidence_excerpt: Abstract: 'We prove the C^{0,1}_loc-inextendibility of weak null singularities without any symmetry assumptions. The proof introduces a new strategy to infer C^{0,1}_loc-inextendibility from the blow-up of curvature. The assumed blow-up is expected to be satisfied for weak null singularities in the interior of generic rotating black holes. Thus, we expect the result presented here to directly contribute to the resolution of the C^{0,1}_loc-formulation of the strong cosmic censorship conjecture in a neighbourhood of subextremal Kerr.'
